anomaly_def.Name: MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite definition: The database is simultaneously affected by unchecked growth of obsolete MVCC row versions/rollback records and by depletion of available disk or tablespace capacity; the version store inflates faster than it can be cleaned while free space shrinks toward a hard boundary.

Combined observable phenomena: free-space monitoring shows a steep, unexplained drop that coincides with sharply rising counts of dead tuples and rollback segments; data-file auto-extension or tablespace growth requests begin to fail, while VACUUM/PURGE workers run constantly yet report little progress. Sequential scans, index range scans, and visibility checks take longer because of page bloat, and the query planner misestimates row counts. Users may first see "no space left" or "cannot allocate version record" errors, stalled DML statements waiting for space, log-archive back-pressure, and emergency wraparound warnings all at once, making the root cause appear as a generalized outage rather than two specific issues.

Causal interaction: heavy update/delete churn produces a flood of obsolete versions that inflate heap and index pages; this ballooning rapidly consumes remaining disk space and pushes the system into a storage-capacity crisis. Conversely, once free space is scarce, background cleanup cannot allocate the working space it needs to rewrite pages or extend rollback areas, so it falls further behind, allowing even more obsolete versions to accumulate. As space approaches exhaustion, checkpoints and log archiving stall, which in turn prolongs active snapshots and prevents version pruning—creating a positive feedback loop that amplifies both anomalies and accelerates system degradation.

entry.official_description: This member was unable to log the View_change_log_event into the binary log, hence it will leave the group. Please check that there is available disk space and add the member back to the group.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with file creation, filesystem access, write durability, log persistence, tablespace management, or storage-capacity boundaries.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect filesystem capacity and permissions, verify persistence paths, review log and data placement, and check whether storage latency or write failures are affecting the engine.
